pelage_geometry_and_topology.patch_morphology: Irregular polygonal dark regions with high-contrast, sharp-edged pixel gradients. Patches on the upper torso display larger relative spatial area, while patches toward the lower flank and hindquarters are smaller with higher edge complexity and serration.
pelage_geometry_and_topology.corridor_network: Continuous network of light-colored interstitial pathways. Junction nodes primarily feature tri-radial and quadri-radial intersections. Pathway thickness is relatively consistent across the mid-section but narrows significantly toward the lower legs.

dorsal_ridge_profile.edge_serration: Low-amplitude, high-frequency serrated mane profile visible along the upper neck, appearing as a dark, jagged boundary against the background.
dorsal_ridge_profile.contour_gaps: A structural interruption in the continuous mane line is visible at the shoulder transition, coinciding with the position of a perched avian subject.

focal_dorsal_anomalies.chronic_feeding_lesions: Multiple raised, nodular protrusions (approximately 5-8 visible) are distributed across the mid-to-upper flank, characterized by localized textural disruption and shadowing.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Presence of numerous distinct, circular skin nodules or raised lesions across the lateral torso, indicating widespread textural irregularity.
other_distinctive_markers: Three avian organisms (oxpeckers) are perched on the dorsal ridge and posterior flank regions of the subject.
